description:
Manage Settings

Update company configuration — the consolidated settings writer.

Actions (no ids — settings are singletons per company):
- offer_publish: make an offer public (id = offer UUID). First fetch
  type='offer_publication', then review its exact facts. Payload:
  {expected_version: preview.version, facts: preview.facts}. Owner/operator
  approval publishes these facts for buyers and agents, including discovery
  and incoming inquiries. Third-party copies cannot be recalled.
- offer_withdraw: make an offer private (id = offer UUID;
  payload = {expected_version}). Revokes its buyer sessions too.
- buyer_inquiry_decide: review a buyer inquiry (id = inquiry UUID;
  payload = {expected_version: action_version, decision: reply|decline,
  reply?: exact reviewed text}). Reply appears only in the buyer session.
- profile: update the company profile / ICP (`payload` = the profile
  fields; this steers research match scoring). If supplied, `industry`
  must be one CanonicalIndustry value: Agriculture, Construction,
  Consumer Goods, Consumer Services, Education, Energy & Utilities,
  Financial Services, Government, Healthcare, Hospitality & Travel,
  Legal Services, Manufacturing, Marketing & Advertising,
  Media & Entertainment, Nonprofit, Professional Services, Real Estate,
  Retail & E-commerce, Software & Technology, Staffing & Recruiting,
  Telecommunications, Transportation & Logistics, Wholesale & Distribution,
  or Other. Provider labels and Unspecified are rejected.
- auto_fill: AI-fill the company profile from the website (`payload`
  optional: {website_url?}; returns a job to poll via
  fetch type='job').
- automation: update workspace automation settings (`payload` = the
  automation fields, including the per-workspace diagnosis switch
  diagnosis_loop_disabled, and impact_verifier_default: who verifies
  customer impact on new promises, {roles, customer_confirmation_required};
  the role agent verifies only from the customer's own words and needs
  customer_confirmation_required=true and a human role beside it;
  owners and operators only).
- marketing: update LinkedIn marketing settings (`payload` = the
  marketing fields).
- cta_link: manage call-to-action links (`payload` = {action:
  create|update|delete, cta_link_id?, name?, url?, cta_type?,
  is_active?}).
- offer_create: add a live offer to the catalog objectives sell from
  (`payload` = {name, pricing_type?: fixed|commission|hybrid|custom,
  list_price_minor?, currency?, billing_period?, commission_rate_bps?,
  commission_basis?, pricing_notes?, description?, monetization_model?}).
  Fixed/hybrid require a minor-unit price (zero means free); commission/custom
  omit price and period. Commission rate may be unknown; a stated rate is
  1–10000 basis points (100 = 1%) and requires its revenue basis. Custom
  requires pricing_notes. Hybrid is a base fee plus commission.
  Monetary forecasts require fixed pricing or separate agreed deal terms.
- offer_update: edit a live offer (id = offer UUID; `payload` = {name?, description?}).
  Economic terms are immutable; retire and create a successor to change them.
- offer_retire: retire an offer no live objective sells (id = offer UUID;
  no payload); the name frees for a new live offer.
- view_save: save a private view of the Accounts, People or Deals table
  (`payload` = {tab: accounts|people|deals, name, definition: {params}}).
  params are the table's URL keys: accounts q, industry, account_list,
  research_objective, owner (me | member id), open_deals (yes|no), sort,
  dir, cols; people q, objective, research (researched|stub),
  account_list, list, stage, enrollment (enrolled|paused|stopped), score
  (60- | -39 | 40-59), added (7d|30d|90d|365d), persona, sort, dir, cols;
  deals q, scope, pipeline, stage (a stage label), owner, sort, dir.
  Returns the view with `url`, which opens it. List views with fetch
  type='settings' subtype='record_views' filters={tab}. Sharing with
  the workspace is the person's choice in the table's View menu.
- view_update: rename or redefine one of the caller's private views
  (id = view id; `payload` = {expected_revision, name?, definition?}).
  A shared view is refused (403): its people change it from the View menu.
- hubspot_sync_settings: set the custom HubSpot contact properties to
  mirror into company_people.custom_fields (`payload` =
  {extra_contact_properties: [...]}); CHANGING the list auto-enqueues a
  full backfill so existing contacts pick up the new attributes.
- hubspot_backfill: kick a full HubSpot re-pull for this company (owners
  → companies → pipelines → contacts → deals → lists → engagements). No
  payload. Heavy (hours at 250k+ contacts). The recovery path when
  contacts were imported before their custom properties were configured.
  Operators target a client with `for_company`.
Team objective-delegation grant/revoke moved to manage_outreach
(objective_delegate / objective_revoke_delegation, VRU-878).

Payloads are validated by the underlying route's own schema, so a bad
field returns that route's precise 422.

### Responses:

**200**: Successful Response (Success Response)
Content-Type: application/json

action.description: The operation to perform — see the tool description for the action vocabulary and each action's id/payload semantics.
action.title: action

for_company.description: Optional company ID or name (UUID, or case-insensitive EXACT name match — partial / substring matches are NOT supported; ambiguous names raise 400) to execute this tool as. Use get_operator_companies, or get_operator_overview with view='companies', to list available companies. Only needed if you manage multiple companies. Access is enforced server-side: the tool resolves the value to a user_company_id and verifies the caller's membership in `company_users` — a 403 'Company not found or access denied' means EITHER the value did not match a known company OR the caller is not a member of it. The MCP operator role itself is NOT auto-granted — operators get this access by being members of each client company via `company_users` (the same row that grants any normal user access).
for_company.title: for_company

id.description: Target entity id, or an ARRAY of ids to apply the same action+payload to each (max 100; see the tool description for which entity the id names per action).
id.title: id

items.description: For create-like actions only: an array of per-item payloads processed in order with per-item results (max 100). Mutually exclusive with `id` and `payload`.
items.title: items

payload.description: Action-specific fields, validated by the underlying route's own schema (a bad field 422s with that route's precise errors). See the tool description per action.
payload.title: payload
